title: System Explorer host findings
description: Every warn/critical opinion this host currently derives, one record per (object, opinion key) — the identity the hub's findings registry attaches lifecycle to (SPEC rule 15, section 6.3). `unobserved` names every collection that would have been swept and could not be, with its reason: a consumer may treat a finding's absence as resolution only for collections not listed there. Shared $defs are duplicated from observation.schema.json deliberately so each schema file is standalone.

locators.description: Every locator this process fronts — the affirmative scope of the unobserved statement. A consumer may treat a finding's absence as resolution only for locators listed here (falling back to the envelope host when absent), so a mixed host+app process states exactly which identities its sweep covered.

unobserved.description: Collections that could not be evaluated this sweep, each with the reason. Explicitly empty means everything evaluable was evaluated.

host.description: The locator this entry narrows to, when it is not the envelope's (an app adapter in a mixed process).

timing.description: What producing this answer cost the host that answered — added 0.6, after the estate measured the agent from OUTSIDE and found one findings sweep burning 2.4 s of CPU on a single-core host, three quarters of that agent's standing bill, with nothing in the product able to say so. wall_ms is elapsed; cpu_ms is THIS process's user+system time across the span; child_cpu_ms is its reaped children's, which is where most of an adapter's cost lives (zpool, nft and lsblk burn their own, charged to the cgroup and absent from this process's own figure) — the split says whether a slow answer is arithmetic here or somebody else's program. Absent from an agent predating the field; never stored, because history snapshots items rather than envelopes and a figure that differs every request would otherwise churn /v1/changes into noise. On a SWEEP the per-subsystem figures are WALL ONLY and they overlap: subsystems run concurrently in one process, so they sum to more than the sweep took and process CPU across the sweep belongs to the sweep and cannot be split between them. A per-adapter CPU column would be a number nobody can produce. rss_bytes and peak_rss_bytes are the agent's own memory, deliberately not broken down by adapter — Python offers the runtime no per-object ownership to attribute, and a plausible split would be invention.

host.description: The locator this finding's identity keys under, when it is not the envelope's (an app adapter in a mixed process) — it must match what the same object's collection and evidence envelopes declare.

evidence_ref.description: The pointer back to the object that can prove or refute this finding right now (section 6.3's read side).

look.description: Where to look next, carried verbatim from the row's opinion: collection routes on the agent that raised this finding. Routes are agent-relative, like evidence_ref. See observation.schema.json for why this is not a filter.

fact.description: The fact that ORDERS the answer at that route. Absent when no single fact ranks it.

label.description: The human phrase the link is worded with.
